data.narrative:
Armada, a Series B space and aerospace company founded by Dan Wright and Jon Runyan, has raised $186M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 4 private peers at the same or adjacent stage (Sierra Space, Cowboy Space Corporation, Aalyria, and Skyryse) and 5 public Space & Aerospace equities (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL).

Two methods triangulate on Armada's value. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.9x multiplier to the $186M raised-to-date proxy, implying $353M. The peer-median method anchors to 4 same-sector comparables with a median valuation of $1.6B, though this cohort spans a wide range from $1.1B to $8.0B. Public-comp anchoring cannot be applied absent revenue disclosure. The two applicable methods yield a low of $300M, a median of $1.0B, and a high of $1.9B.

The stage-progression floor reflects limited venture equity deployed; the peer-median ceiling reflects Armada's positioning relative to Series B and Series C peers. The valuation range is substantively driven by uncertainty around Armada's revenue trajectory and competitive positioning within a heterogeneous peer set. Public-comp P/S multiples (27.4x median) suggest material upside if revenue justifies such multiples, but lack of financial disclosure precludes quantitative application. Key uncertainties center on Armada's unit economics, market share capture, and technical differentiation relative to the named peer group.
